subject: general
question: In which year was the Steel Authority of India Ltd incorporated?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1973**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Steel Authority of India Ltd (SAIL)** was incorporated on 24th January 1973.
 
• SAIL is one of the largest steel-making companies in India and one of the Maharatnas of the country's Central Public Sector Enterprises.
 
• It operates and owns 5 integrated steel plants at Bhilai, Rourkela, Durgapur, Bokaro, and Burnpur (Asansol) and 3 special steel plants at Salem, Durgapur, and Bhadravathi.
 
• SAIL traces its origins to the Hindustan Steel Limited (HSL) which was set up in 1954, with which it was merged later on to form a single entity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maharatna Status:**

 
 
• The Maharatna status is the highest recognition for public sector enterprises in India.
 
• It allows greater autonomy for investment and operations compared to other public sector enterprises.
 
• To qualify as a Maharatna, a company must have an annual turnover of more than Rs 25,000 crore, net profit after tax of more than Rs 5,000 crore, and a significant global presence.
 
 
 
• **Integrated Steel Plants:**
 
 
• An integrated steel plant is a factory where all the processes required for steel production are carried out from raw material handling to finished steel production.
 
• These processes include melting, casting, rolling, and finishing.
 
• SAIL's integrated steel plants are located at various strategic locations across India, enhancing its production capacity and market reach.
 
 
 
• **Public Sector Enterprises:**
 
 
• Public Sector Enterprises (PSEs) are companies in which the majority of the equity is owned by the government.
 
• They play a crucial role in the economic development of a country by contributing to GDP, employment, and industrialization.
 
• In India, PSEs are classified into Maharatna, Navratna, and Miniratna based on their performance and scale of operations.
